clause_i.reason: For the same prior action history and task times, generated island worlds can be reflected and can differ in landing side, gap, well position, and contact-induced velocity. At a coasting stage the delayed-optimal body correction therefore differs between otherwise identical I_t histories; an observation-free q cannot choose the required side or shape action for every history in C_Delta(D).

clause_ii.reason: The bounded 80 ms window contains three chronological frames, while the canvas visibly renders the solids, seals, parcel rectangle, and parcel-attached controls. Consecutive parcel positions expose the sign and magnitude of coasting velocity and its clearance from the receiving opening, so g can select the lateral counter-hold or morph action that is optimal at the 160 ms delayed endpoint.

clause_iii.reason: Use a reachable tall parcel at h=200 (width=6400/200=32) moving toward an L5 receiving-opening edge. The opening is 52-60 units wide, leaving only 10-14 units of center margin. With neutral control after release, the physics still updates vx and x; at the speed cap, two ticks/80 ms move the parcel about 8 units while it remains recoverable, making the same counter-slide action strictly less effective than at t, and four ticks/160 ms can consume the margin. This loss is caused by visible non-clock x/vx evolution, not by a deadline or later completion.

common_visible_process: Unsupported or released-parcel physics: the parcel's position and motion change autonomously on the canvas under inertial coasting and gravity. The same visible trajectory in the recent frames determines which full-mode correction is appropriate at the delayed endpoint and simultaneously consumes the narrow landing/opening clearance, so the relevant action opportunity degrades while waiting.

pre_run.reason: At L5 every generated instance uses the island layout with a 140-175 unit gap and a 52-60 unit receiving opening. The area-preserving parcel needs a broad shape to bridge the gap, then a tall/narrow shape (up to h=200, width 32) to reach and enter the upper well. Neutral physics changes position and velocity but never morphs height, and the route therefore requires outcome-affecting morph and steering actions after the run has begun. There is no separate autonomous-start phase in the browser implementation; a no-action passive phase cannot complete the staged all-seal outcome, so at least half of instances cannot admit a successful pre-run solution.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 is the island profile with island_width 170, gap 140-175, opening 52-60, clearance 42, reach 185, drag 0.94, and well_clearance 145; full interaction is implemented; the observation window is 80 ms with 3 frames.

The generator applies the supplied difficulty condition, constructs the randomized island/landing/roof geometry and four seal positions, randomly reflects the world, and initializes an active area-6400 parcel with h=80, bottom=420, and zero velocity.

The browser physics preserves area through width=area/h, updates height only from control, applies drag and horizontal movement, applies gravity and landing, collects seals, and terminates on fall, solve, or timeout.
Full mode exposes four body arrows; the animation tick advances from elapsed performance time, pointer release sets [0,0], and body pointer events record holds while the parcel continues to simulate.
The visible room contains the canvas and parcel-attached body-control layout used by the full interaction surface.
The authoritative replay uses the same substep physics and checks the exact generated world, interaction mode, body-hold input source, event transitions, terminal tick, and final physical state.

The reference controller predicts drag/coast, brakes with feedback, and for island worlds performs distinct tall, lateral, flattened, lateral, and tall stages; its module explicitly treats privileged state access as wiring-test evidence.
Task verification loads the exported result and the Concertina Courier replay grader rather than trusting client collection claims.
